item.title: Hungary Narrows Budget Gap to $10.8 Billion After June Surplus
item.description: Hungary narrowed its first-half shortfall after posting the biggest monthly budget surplus since 2010, helping the new government as it takes on one of the biggest fiscal challenges in the European Union.

item.title: US Stock Futures Slide After Trump Says Iran Ceasefire Is Over
item.description: US equity futures fell as investors turned risk averse after President Donald Trump said the tentative ceasefire with Iran has ended, fueling concerns of a renewal in fighting.

item.title: Apple’s Chip Deal With Broadcom Expected to Exceed $30 Billion
item.description: Apple Inc., following through on a pledge to boost spending on US-made components, said its expanded agreement with Broadcom Inc. is expected to top $30 billion.

item.title: French Watchdog Orders Meta Negotiations Over News Copyright
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. was ordered by the French competition watchdog to hold talks with news organizations over copyright payments, following two complaints that the social media giant was abusing its dominant position.

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Extend Loss as Oil Jumps on Iran Risks
item.description: Emerging-market stocks extended losses as an escalation in the Middle East conflict added to the ongoing rotation out of AI beneficiaries.

item.title: Labor Crunch Tests Growth Limits for US Data Center Builders
item.description: Following several quarters of record order books, a skilled-labor shortage is testing the limits of growth for the craft-labor providers who build data centers across the US.

item.title: China Cites Trump Remarks in Rare Criticism of US Taiwan Envoy
item.description: China took the rare step of publicly criticizing the top US diplomat in Taiwan, invoking select remarks by President Donald Trump to argue that the envoy’s actions are destabilizing relations.

item.title: UK Carpet Maker Victoria Signs Deal With Left-Behind Bondholders
item.description: UK carpet maker Victoria Plc and a group of bondholders left behind in an earlier debt deal have struck an agreement over a balance sheet restructuring.

item.title: Nvidia’s $1 Trillion Slide Sends Valuation to Pre-AI Boom Levels
item.description: After losing roughly $1 trillion in market value in less than two months, Nvidia Corp.’s stock is the cheapest it’s been since before the AI boom kicked off and sent the shares into the stratosphere.

item.title: China Allowing Major Exports of Diesel and Gasoline This Month
item.description: Chinese oil refiners have been granted more permits to export gasoline, diesel and jet fuel this month, according to people familiar with the matter, in a major relaxation of restrictions imposed during the Iran war.

item.title: Bolloré Wins Paris Court Ruling Over Vivendi Control Dispute
item.description: Vincent Bolloré won a Paris ruling that — if it survives a further challenge — could end up saving his company billions of euros after judges backed his long-held claim that he didn’t control Vivendi SE before a split of the media conglomerate in 2024.

item.title: Dutch Prosecutor Summons Tata Steel Over Ijmuiden Pollution
item.description: The Dutch Public Prosecution Service has summoned the local Tata Steel subsidiary on suspicion of criminal offenses including intentionally releasing harmful substances, which it said could have consequences for public health.

item.title: Apple Loses Spat With EU Over App Store and iPhone Rules
item.description: Apple Inc. lost a European Union court fight to stop its App Store and iPhone operating system being hit by the full-force of the bloc’s antitrust crackdown on Big Tech.

item.title: European Bonds Slide as Oil Spike Reignites Inflation Fears
item.description: European bonds slumped, sending French borrowing costs to their highest since 2009, as oil prices and inflation expectations rose after President Donald Trump declared an end to the ceasefire with Iran.

item.title: Alphabet Powers 44% Jump in India Foreign Investment, UN Says
item.description: Foreign direct investment in India surged in 2025, driven largely by Alphabet Inc.’s data center project, though a decline in greenfield investments signaled a weaker investment outlook, according to the United Nations’ trade agency.

item.title: India Fat-Loss Drug Sales Slow After Early Spike From Generics
item.description: Growth in India’s obesity- and diabetes-drug market is losing steam just months after a surge triggered by the arrival of generic semaglutide products.

item.title: Euro Bears Return as Surging Oil Prices Test Currency’s Rebound
item.description: Traders are buying insurance against renewed weakness in the euro as climbing crude oil prices threaten last week’s rebound.

item.title: OpenAI to Roll Out Top AI Model Globally After Limited Preview
item.description: OpenAI is set to release its most advanced model widely on Thursday and is expanding its preview globally, the company said.

item.title: Turkey’s $37 Billion Defense Firm Says Foreign Orders Doubled
item.description: Turkey’s $37 billion state-run defense contractor Aselsan Elektronik Sanayi ve Ticaret AS said international orders have doubled in the past year on the back of demand fueled by the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

item.title: Private Placements Surge in Middle East on Iran War Volatility
item.description: Private debt placements from the Middle East are surging as volatility due to the Iran war drives borrowers into alternative markets.

item.title: Netherlands and UK Sign $3.2 Billion Deal on Amphibious Ships
item.description: The Netherlands and the UK signed a £2.4 billion ($3.2 billion) agreement to produce new amphibious transport ships, part of a flurry of deals between European NATO members in Ankara.

item.title: Alibaba Shares Jump Most in 10 Months as Rebound Hopes Grow
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s shares surged the most since September after investors turned optimistic on its earnings and shifted capital into major Chinese internet companies that had lagged the market.

item.title: Temasek Assets Break $400 Billion as AI Bets Boost Returns
item.description: Singaporean state-owned investor Temasek Holdings Pte is ramping up its exposure to artificial intelligence and the Americas, a shift which helped push its net portfolio value to S$518 billion ($401 billion) in the last financial year.

item.title: Uzbek Logistics Firm Centrum Bets on Silk Road Trade Before IPO
item.description: Uzbekistan’s largest private logistics group, Centrum Holding, is preparing for a London initial public offering as soon as next year, while planning an ambitious expansion of operations along trade routes linking Europe and Asia.

item.title: Unite Group Offers Discounted Dorms in Bid to Ramp Up Sales
item.description: The Unite Group Plc has begun offering discounted rents to some students as the landlord looks to boost reservations for the next academic year.

item.title: Vistry Expects £30 Million Pretax Loss, CFO Steps Down
item.description: UK homebuilder Vistry Group Plc expects to report a loss before tax of about £30 million ($40.1 million) in the first half of the year as it races to raise cash.

item.title: AI Chip Startup SambaNova Raises Funds at $11 Billion Valuation
item.description: Chip startup SambaNova Systems Inc. has raised $1 billion at an $11 billion valuation, underscoring investors’ conviction in rising demand for infrastructure tied to artificial intelligence.

item.title: Japan Payment Processor Collapse Hits Banks, Restaurants
item.description: The bankruptcy of Zentoshin Co., an Osaka-based credit card payment processor, threatens both the regional banks which funded it as well as the small and medium-sized restaurants that relied on its services.

item.title: Fertilizer Firm Climbs 18% In Early Trading After Oman IPO
item.description: Oman India Fertiliser Co. jumped about 18% on its Muscat trading debut after raising 261 million Omani rials ($678 million) in the region’s largest initial public offering of the year.

item.title: Blue Owl Buys £1.3 Billion UK Private Hospital Portfolio
item.description: Blue Owl Capital Inc has completed a deal to buy a portfolio of UK private hospitals from Malaysia’s Employees Provident Fund.
